title: VLOOKUP From Another Sheet
description: VLOOKUP from another sheet just needs a sheet prefix. Learn the cross-sheet syntax, quoted sheet names, INDIRECT for dynamic tabs and 3D references in Excel.
intro: Running a VLOOKUP from another sheet is not a special function or a different mode - it is the same VLOOKUP with a sheet name in front of the range. Once you know the sheet prefix rule and how quoted names work, a lookup across tabs is no harder than a lookup in the same column. This guide covers the syntax, the two ways it breaks, XLOOKUP's cleaner alternative, and how to make the source sheet dynamic with INDIRECT.
prerequisites: A workbook with data on more than one sheet

sections.title: Cross-Sheet Syntax in One Line
sections.content: A reference to another sheet is just the sheet name, an exclamation mark, then the range you already know. Drop that in the table_array argument and the search happens on the other sheet while the formula itself stays where you typed it. The result is a normal value - nothing about the cell bring back tells Excel it came from elsewhere.

steps.name: Point at the source sheet
steps.text: Type the sheet name, an exclamation mark, then the cell. Excel switches to that sheet and completes the reference for you.

steps.name: Use the whole other-sheet table as table_array
steps.text: Wrap the range in $ signs so it does not shift when you copy the formula down the column.

example.result: 24.99 - the value from column C of the Products sheet, on the row whose SKU matches A2
example.explanation: A2 holds the SKU you are searching for. Products!$A$2:$D$100 is the table on the other tab, and 3 means return the third column of that table. The FALSE forces an exact match.

tips: Anchor the lookup range with $ - a relative range copied down 500 rows will silently slide off your data.

sections.title: Sheet Names With Spaces Need Quotes
sections.content: If a sheet name contains a space, a hyphen, or begins with a digit, Excel requires single quotes around it. Omitting them is the single most common cause of a cross-sheet #NAME? error, because without quotes Excel tries to read part of the name as a cell address.

example.result: 24.99, pulled from the sheet named Q3 Sales
example.explanation: The apostrophes delimit the name so Excel does not mistake Q3 for a cell reference. In practice you rarely type them: click the other sheet's tab while building the formula and Excel inserts them automatically.

tips: If the sheet name itself contains an apostrophe, double it - 'O''Brien'!A1 is the correct form.

sections.title: XLOOKUP Across Sheets - Cleaner, and Column-Proof
sections.content: XLOOKUP accepts a separate lookup array and return array, so you name each sheet range once and never count columns. That matters in practice: with VLOOKUP, inserting a column in the source sheet breaks every formula that hard-codes an index number.

example.result: 24.99, or the text Not found when the SKU is absent from the Products sheet
example.explanation: A2:A100 is searched and C2:C100 is returned, independently. Adding a column to Products does not change which array is returned, so the formula survives edits that would break VLOOKUP.

tips: Google Sheets also supports XLOOKUP, so this formula works there unchanged; without the fourth argument Sheets returns #N/A instead of a friendly message.

sections.title: INDIRECT - When the Source Sheet Changes at Runtime
sections.content: Sometimes the sheet you look into is not fixed: one tab per month, per region or per salesperson, chosen by the user. INDIRECT reads a text string and turns it into a live range, so the sheet name can come from a cell or a dropdown.

example.result: 24.99 when B1 contains the text Products; the same formula reads the March sheet as soon as B1 says March
example.explanation: The & operator assembles the string 'Products'!$A$2:$D$100 from the sheet name in B1, and INDIRECT converts that text into a real reference. Two caveats: INDIRECT is volatile, so it recalculates on every change, and it cannot read a workbook that is closed.

tips: The dropdown entries must match the sheet names exactly, capitals included, or INDIRECT returns #REF!.

sections.title: 3D References, and When Not to Cross Sheets
sections.content: If the same cell sits in the same position on many consecutive sheets, Excel can read across all of them at once. This is called a 3D reference, and it is excellent for aggregates - but it cannot power a lookup, because there is no single table to search.

example.result: Adds cell B2 on every sheet from Jan through Dec, in sheet-tab order
example.explanation: Aggregates such as SUM, AVERAGE and COUNT accept 3D references; VLOOKUP does not. For lookups across dozens of tabs, consolidate the data into one table first and point VLOOKUP at that - the formula stays readable and recalculates far faster.

tips: Google Sheets has no 3D reference across tabs, so each sheet must be named explicitly there.

functionsUsed.name: VLOOKUP
functionsUsed.description: VLOOKUP (Vertical Lookup) is a built-in function in Excel and Google Sheets that searches for a value in the first column of a table and returns a value in the same row from a specified column.

functionsUsed.name: XLOOKUP
functionsUsed.description: XLOOKUP is the modern replacement for VLOOKUP. It searches a range or array for a value and returns the corresponding item from a second range or array. It supports exact and approximate matching, wildcards, and can search in any direction.

functionsUsed.name: INDIRECT
functionsUsed.description: INDIRECT converts a text string into a cell reference that Excel can use in a formula.

summary: Looking up a value on another sheet is the same VLOOKUP with the sheet name and an exclamation mark in front of the range: =VLOOKUP(A2, Products!$A$2:$D$100, 3, FALSE). Quote the sheet name if it contains spaces, anchor the table range with $, and remember that Excel inserts the quotes for you when you build the formula by clicking the other tab. For anything long-lived, prefer XLOOKUP with two named arrays, and reach for INDIRECT only when the source sheet genuinely varies at runtime.
